y-m-32-02.prereq.2: (Assumption) H1 here only means difficulty/support, not grade curriculum. Assumed intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit after middle school multiplication formulas, factoring, quadratic basics.
y-m-32-02.title: Make a cubic expression yourself that meets two conditions
y-m-32-02.topic: Make a polynomial using remainders and factors (undetermined coefficients)
y-m-32-02.goal: Make several cubic expressions meeting the conditions, and distinguish what is fixed from what is free given the counts of conditions and unknowns.
y-m-32-02.material: You want a cubic f(x)=x³+ax²+bx+c, where a, b, c are integers (ax² means a times x squared). Conditions: ① f(x) is divisible by x−1. ② Dividing f(x) by x+1 leaves remainder 4. Also a and c are not 0, so both quadratic and constant terms appear.
y-m-32-02.thinking.0: Turn conditions into equations and make several examples that satisfy them
y-m-32-02.thinking.1: Understand that too few conditions do not determine one solution
y-m-32-02.thinking.2: Tell fixed values apart from free values
y-m-32-02.prereq.0: Remainder on dividing a polynomial by x−k equals its value at x=k (intro high-school Common Math polynomial topic)
y-m-32-02.prereq.1: Solve two linear equations with letters as a system (middle-school level)
y-m-32-02.s.s1.prompt: There are 2 conditions but 3 unknowns, a, b, c. About how many f(x) can meet them?
y-m-32-02.s.s1.hint.0: For conditions ① and ②, decide which x value to substitute in each.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.hint.1: Substitute those values into f(x) to make 2 equations in a, b, c; compare equations and unknowns.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.o.a: There are only 2 conditions, so some numbers remain unknown and we can't make such a cubic.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.r.a: Few conditions don't make it impossible. Contradictory conditions would.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.o.b: If conditions are given, f is always determined as one answer; just calculate it.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.r.b: With 3 unknowns and 2 conditions, check whether everything is determined.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.o.c: If conditions don't contradict, some freedom remains, so you can make several.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.r.c: This judgment compares conditions and unknowns to see if any freedom remains.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.o.d: Any integers you choose for a, b, c meet the conditions regardless.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.r.d: You must satisfy conditions ① and ②. Substitute values to check.
y-m-32-02.s.s1.explain: If the conditions don't contradict, 2 equations can't determine all 3 unknowns, so something remains free. Make examples to find how many are determined.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different (a, b, c) meeting ①, ②, and 'a and c are not 0'.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.hint.0: First write the required values when substituting 1 and −1 for x.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.hint.1: Choose a value for a, then adjust b and c to satisfy both conditions.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.hint.2: Substitute your (a, b, c) into f(1) and f(−1) to check.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.fail.c1: a, b, c must be integers.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.fail.c2: f(1) isn't 0. Substitute 1 for x and calculate.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.ok.c3: Remainder on division by x+1 is 4 (f(−1)=4).
y-m-32-02.s.s2.fail.c3: Remainder on division by x+1 isn't 4. Substitute −1 for x and calculate.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.fail.c4: a and c must not be 0.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.explain: From f(1)=1+a+b+c=0 and f(−1)=−1+a−b+c=4, we get b=−3 and a+c=2. So b is fixed at −3; once a is chosen, c=2−a. Examples: (1, −3, 1), (3, −3, −1), (−2, −3, 4). Exclude a=2, c=0 because c must not be 0.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.prompt: Compare your examples: a and c had many possible values, but b had one. Explain why in your own words.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write the two conditions as equations in a, b, c; add and subtract the equations.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.hint.1: Compare which letter remains after adding and after subtracting.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.placeholder: Example: Writing the conditions as equations gives ...
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Did you write both conditions as equations in a, b, c?
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: Did you explain separately why b is fixed and a and c are free?
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: Did you check all your examples satisfy a+c=2?
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.model.0: The equations are a+b+c=−1 and a−b+c=5. Subtracting fixes b=−3; adding leaves a+c=2. Choose a and c follows, so they have many possible values.
y-m-32-02.s.s2.because.model.1: b=−3 is fixed because subtracting leaves only b. The remaining condition is a+c=2, so any integer pair summing to 2 works, such as 1 and 1, or 3 and −1.

y-m-32-04.prereq.2: (Assumption) H1 here only means difficulty/support, not grade curriculum. Assumed intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit after middle school multiplication formulas, factoring, quadratic basics.
y-m-32-04.title: Can the expansion be wrong even though the check passed?
y-m-32-04.topic: Multiplication formulas: square of a sum of 3 terms and limits of checking
y-m-32-04.goal: Find the wrong line in an expansion, use a counterexample to show why numeric checking missed the error, then choose a more reliable check.
y-m-32-04.material: This is Hayun's expansion of (x+2y−1)² and numeric check. (x and y are real; y² means y squared, and 2y means 2 times y.) Use (A+B+C)²=A²+B²+C²+2AB+2BC+2CA with A=x, B=2y, C=−1.
y-m-32-04.thinking.1: Make a counterexample to an error the check missed
y-m-32-04.thinking.2: Evaluate the strategy of choosing test values
y-m-32-04.prereq.0: Read expansion of (A+B+C)² (multiplication formula; intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit)
y-m-32-04.prereq.1: Find an expression value by substituting numbers for letters
y-m-32-04.s.s1.prompt: In Hayun's work, choose the first line with a calculation error.
y-m-32-04.s.s1.hint.0: Substitute original B, C, A into 2BC and 2CA and recalculate each.
y-m-32-04.s.s1.hint.1: For each line, tell whether it copies the previous result or calculates something new.
y-m-32-04.s.s1.line.5: Check: x=1, y=1 gives left (1+2−1)²=4 and right 1+4+1+4−2−4=4. They match, so it is correct.
y-m-32-04.s.s1.explain: Line 4 is wrong. 2BC=2·2y·(−1)=−4y and 2CA=2·(−1)·x=−2x. Coefficients −2 and −4 were swapped. Line 5 carries this forward; line 6's arithmetic check is right but cannot catch the error.
y-m-32-04.s.s2.prompt: For Hayun's final x²+4y²+1+4xy−2y−4x to differ from original (x+2y−1)², find 3 pairs (x,y) giving different values.
y-m-32-04.s.s2.hint.0: Try one case with the same number for x and y and one with different numbers; substitute in both expressions and compare.
y-m-32-04.s.s2.hint.1: In example where values differ, check which term makes difference.
y-m-32-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Choose x,y with absolute value no more than 20.
y-m-32-04.s.s2.ok.c2: Expression values differ, so Hayun mistake appear.
y-m-32-04.s.s2.fail.c2: Expression values same, so mistake not found. Try other values.
y-m-32-04.s.s2.explain: Difference between original and Hayun expression na 2x−2y. If x=y, difference 0 and values same; mistake hidden. Choose x≠y, e.g. (0,1): original gives 1, Hayun expression 3. [0 1]
y-m-32-04.s.s3.prompt: What best reason Hayun check (x=1,y=1) miss error, and how better check next time?
y-m-32-04.s.s3.hint.0: At x=1,y=1, calculate −2y−4x and −4y−2x and compare.
y-m-32-04.s.s3.hint.1: When x,y different, check again if both values same.
y-m-32-04.s.s3.o.a: Check calculation wrong; calculator fix this error
y-m-32-04.s.s3.r.a: Check calculation itself right. Think if chosen values caused issue.
y-m-32-04.s.s3.o.b: Because x=y, two wrong terms became same. Try other values too
y-m-32-04.s.s3.r.b: Na thinking say one match no prove am; strengthen check with different values.
y-m-32-04.s.s3.o.c: Plugging values cannot check if expansion correct
y-m-32-04.s.s3.r.c: Plugging numbers fit catch mistakes. Choice of numbers matters.
y-m-32-04.s.s3.o.d: One check enough; this just coincidence unrelated to calculation
y-m-32-04.s.s3.r.d: One match no prove expansion correct. It can match even with error.
y-m-32-04.s.s3.explain: When x=y, wrong term −2y−4x and correct term −4y−2x same. Choose x and y different to expose error. One match no proof; only means “no error found”.

y-m-32-05.prereq.2: (Assumption) H1 here only means difficulty/support, not grade curriculum. Assumed intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit after middle school multiplication formulas, factoring, quadratic basics.
y-m-32-05.title: If one value known, remainder fixed?
y-m-32-05.topic: Remainder after dividing by linear vs quadratic expression: is info sufficient?
y-m-32-05.goal: Judge if given info determine remainder, identify what extra info needed if not, and make counterexample to plausible-but-insufficient info.
y-m-32-05.material: Find remainder when polynomial f(x) divided by (x−1)(x−2). Only fact f(1)=3 known. Remainder degree 1 or lower, so write ax+b, a,b real. Thus f(x)=(x−1)(x−2)Q(x)+ax+b. (Q quotient.)
y-m-32-05.thinking.1: Show with several examples that value not determined
y-m-32-05.thinking.2: Use counterexample to explain why plausible extra info insufficient
y-m-32-05.prereq.0: Remainder of f(x) divided by x−k is f(k); division equation f=(divisor)(quotient)+(remainder) (intro high-school polynomial unit)
y-m-32-05.prereq.1: Remainder dividing by quadratic can be ax+b, degree 1 or less
y-m-32-05.s.s1.prompt: Make 3 different remainders ax+b consistent with f(1)=3.
y-m-32-05.s.s1.hint.0: First check which term disappear when x=1 in division equation.
y-m-32-05.s.s1.ok.c1: Putting x=1 gives value 3, consistent with f(1)=3.
y-m-32-05.s.s1.fail.c1: At x=1, a+b must be 3. Right now it's not 3.
y-m-32-05.s.s1.explain: At x=1, (x−1)(x−2)Q(x)=0, so f(1)=a+b. Therefore all (a,b) with a+b=3 possible. Remainder could be 3, x+2, 3x, −2x+5, and many others. f(1) alone no determine remainder.
y-m-32-05.s.s2.prompt: Besides f(1)=3, what extra info enough to determine remainder uniquely? Choose all.
y-m-32-05.s.s2.hint.0: Change x value in division equation; find value making quotient term disappear.
y-m-32-05.s.s2.hint.1: Write expression in a,b for f at that value, and count if we get two equations. [2]
y-m-32-05.s.s2.r.a: At x=0, quotient term Q(0) remains. Can we know that term?
y-m-32-05.s.s2.o.b: Remainder when f(x) divided by x−2
y-m-32-05.s.s2.r.b: Does this tell remainder ax+b value at x=2?
y-m-32-05.s.s2.r.c: Are a,b fixed just by knowing degree?
y-m-32-05.s.s2.r.d: The different remainders earlier all fit f(1)=3.
y-m-32-05.s.s2.r.e: At x=2, does quotient term disappear?
y-m-32-05.s.s2.r.f: Would knowing quotient degree fix remainder value?
y-m-32-05.s.s2.explain: At x=2, (x−1)(x−2)Q=0, so f(2)=2a+b. Together with f(1)=a+b, determine a,b uniquely. f(2) same as “remainder when divided by x−2”. f(0) still includes Q(0), so no direct b.
y-m-32-05.s.s3.prompt: Two polynomials f₁=x²−2x+4 and f₂=2x²−3x+4 both meet f(0)=4 and f(1)=3. Find remainder for each divided by (x−1)(x−2), compare, explain why remainder not fixed even if f(0) known. [0 1 3 4]
y-m-32-05.s.s3.hint.0: Write division equations for f₁,f₂ with divisor x²−3x+2 (quotient is x² coefficient).
y-m-32-05.s.s3.hint.1: Put x=0 in both equations and compare quotient-multiplied term.
y-m-32-05.s.s3.placeholder: e.g. f₁ remainder ..., f₂ remainder ..., so ...
y-m-32-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You check division of f₁ and f₂ by divisor (x−1)(x−2)?
y-m-32-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You connect why f(0) not directly b of remainder with quotient?
y-m-32-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You conclude “not fixed” from different remainders?
y-m-32-05.s.s3.model.0: f₁ remainder x+2, f₂ remainder 3x, different. Both f(0)=4 and f(1)=3 but remainders differ, so f(0) alone no determine. f(0) includes quotient at 0, not just b.
y-m-32-05.s.s3.model.1: f₁=(x−1)(x−2)·1+(x+2), f₂=(x−1)(x−2)·2+3x. Quotients 1 and 2 differ. At x=0, quotient terms are 2 and 4; remainder constants b are 2 and 0. Both sums 4, so f(0) same; remainder not fixed. [0]

y-m-32-07.prereq.2: (Assumption) H1 here only means difficulty/support, not grade curriculum. Assumed intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit after middle school multiplication formulas, factoring, quadratic basics.
y-m-32-07.title: Is cube of sum same as sum of cubes?
y-m-32-07.topic: Multiplication formula (a+b)³ and when it holds
y-m-32-07.goal: Work out when “cube of sum equals sum of cubes” holds, make examples, and explain condition via expansion.
y-m-32-07.material: Chaewon thinks (a+b)³=a³+b³. Her evidence: substitute a=1,b=0; left (1+0)³=1, right 1³+0³=1. (a,b real; read (a+b)³ “cube of a plus b”.)
y-m-32-07.thinking.1: Make examples where it works and find pattern
y-m-32-07.prereq.1: If product is 0, at least one factor is 0
y-m-32-07.s.s1.prompt: What you think of Chaewon evidence (a=1,b=0)?
y-m-32-07.s.s1.hint.0: Would plugging another number than 0 for b give same as a=1,b=0?
y-m-32-07.s.s1.hint.1: Choose pair with b≠0 and calculate both sides.
y-m-32-07.s.s1.o.a: I found one pair that works, fine to say it works
y-m-32-07.s.s1.o.b: One pair not enough; test other pairs too
y-m-32-07.s.s1.r.b: This points out result for one pair no represent all.
y-m-32-07.s.s1.o.c: If b=0, both sides equal for any a, so test weak. Test b≠0 pairs
y-m-32-07.s.s1.r.c: This judgment considers how much information test gives, whether easy to pass.
y-m-32-07.s.s1.r.d: Size of a no decide test strength. Which values expose difference?
y-m-32-07.s.s1.explain: If b=0, both sides a³ whatever a; weak test. But one pair not enough is also right.
y-m-32-07.s.s1.acc.0: Good to notice b=0 is weak. Better say one pair also not enough.
y-m-32-07.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different nonzero (a,b) pairs where (a+b)³=a³+b³. (a=2,b=−2 and reverse count same.) [0 0 2 2]
y-m-32-07.s.s2.hint.0: Choose nonzero a, change b, calculate both sides.
y-m-32-07.s.s2.hint.1: Table relationship between a,b in working pairs.
y-m-32-07.s.s2.fail.c2: Both sides not equal. Calculate each separately.
y-m-32-07.s.s2.explain: (a+b)³−a³−b³=3ab(a+b). With a,b nonzero, this equals zero only if a+b=0. Thus b=−a. Examples: (1,−1),(2,−2),(5,−5). [0 0 0]
y-m-32-07.s.s2.because.prompt: Write common pattern of your pairs and explain with expansion why only these work.
y-m-32-07.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write at least 3 working pairs and calculate a+b.
y-m-32-07.s.s2.because.placeholder: e.g. My pairs all ... Expansion gives ...
y-m-32-07.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You say why write difference as product?
y-m-32-07.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: You mention why a≠0,b≠0 condition needed?
y-m-32-07.s.s2.because.model.0: All my pairs have a+b=0, i.e. b=−a. Expand (a+b)³=a³+3a²b+3ab²+b³, so difference=3ab(a+b). If a,b nonzero, zero only when a+b=0. [0 0]
y-m-32-07.s.s2.because.model.1: They are opposite-sign same-size numbers (like 2 and −2). Difference simplifies to 3ab(a+b), so if ab≠0, then a+b=0.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.prompt: If you remove condition 'a≠0, b≠0', which (a, b) pairs satisfy (a+b)³=a³+b³?
y-m-32-07.s.s3.hint.0: Think about each factor in difference between both sides, 3ab(a+b), becoming 0.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.hint.1: Check which factor na 0 for a=1,b=0 and a=1,b=−1.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.o.a: E hold only for pairs with b=−a, and no other pair.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.r.a: Remember say Chaewon first pair a=1,b=0 work.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.o.b: E hold only when a=b, no other pair.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.r.b: Put a=b=1 and calculate both sides.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.o.c: Pairs where a=0 or b=0 or a+b=0
y-m-32-07.s.s3.r.c: This judgment gather all cases wey make difference 3ab(a+b) equal 0.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.o.d: E hold for every pair, no pair wey fail fit exist.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.r.d: You already find pairs wey no work earlier.
y-m-32-07.s.s3.explain: For (a+b)³−a³−b³=3ab(a+b)=0, at least one of a=0, b=0, a+b=0 gats hold. Chaewon first pair (1, 0) na case where b=0.

y-m-32-01.title: If equation works for some values, does it always work?
y-m-32-01.topic: Identity meaning: how many values can settle it?
y-m-32-01.goal: Separate evidence from substitutions for "few values" versus "all x", and adjust confidence as new info comes.
y-m-32-01.material: Seoa sees x³=x and says substituting 0,1,−1 keeps working, so equation holds for every x. (x³ cubed; x real.) Check with values one at a time. 0 1
y-m-32-01.thinking.0: Adjust confidence step by step as evidence grows
y-m-32-01.thinking.1: Explore difference between proving true and disproving it
y-m-32-01.prereq.1: Identity means equation true for every x (intro high-school polynomial unit)
y-m-32-01.prereq.2: (Assumption) H1 here only means difficulty/support, not grade curriculum. Assumed intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit after middle school multiplication formulas, factoring, quadratic basics.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.prompt: Info arrives step by step. Each time choose what you think of Seoa claim.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.hint.0: Count values tested so far and untested values remaining.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.hint.1: Before next info, say if your confidence grew or shrank compared with earlier judgment.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.info: Put x=0: left 0³=0, right 0, equal. Put x=1: left 1³=1, right 1, equal.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.ask: What think of Seoa claim from only these 2 values?
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.after: x=0 and 1 no contradict claim, but no guarantee all x. Keep possibility open and test others.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.o.a: It worked for 2 values, so conclude every x without more tests.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Some values working no same as all; untested values may fail.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Could be true, but 2 values cannot settle it; test more.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This considers both tested count and how far from all x.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Same at 0 and 1 is coincidence; test tells nothing.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.r.c: It working is information, just not enough to settle.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.o.d: If works twice, naturally same for untested values.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You decide untested outcome in advance. Need evidence.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.info: I also put x=−1. Left (−1)³=−1, right −1, equal. Now all 3 values 0,1,−1 work. 0 1
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.after: Both judgments reasonable. More successes raise confidence somewhat, but no prove all x. Could suspect special values chosen.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.o.a: 0,1,−1 easy special values; test 2 or 3 too. 0 1
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This considers what kind values tested.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.o.b: It works for 3 values in row, now certain for all x.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Working 3 times no guarantee remaining values.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Because 3 work, less likely it is an identity.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.r.c: More values work and no reason yet to move opposite direction.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.o.d: More likely now, but not settled.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Confidence rose as evidence grew, but we still kept confidence separate from being certain.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.info: Putting x=2 gives 2³=8 on left and 2 on right, so they differ.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.ask: What can we say about Seoa's claim?
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.after: At x=2, 8≠2, so x³=x is not an identity. To prove it, every x must work; one value can disprove it.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.o.a: It worked for 3 values and failed for only 1, so it is almost an identity.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You don't judge 'works for every x' by what fraction of trials worked.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Treat x=2 as an exception and call it an identity because it works for 0, 1, and −1.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Removing the exception changes the claim 'every x'.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Maybe it's a calculation mistake, so leave out this value and delay judgment.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Calculate 8 and 2 directly. Once checked, the judgment is settled.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.o.d: At x=2 both sides differ, so it isn't an identity. One value is enough.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.st.2.r.d: To disprove 'every', one failing value is enough.
y-m-32-01.s.s1.reflect: How did your confidence change for the first 2 values, the third, and x=2? Say in one sentence when testing values is enough and when it isn't.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.prompt: What best explains why x³=x works for x=0, 1, −1 but not x=2?
y-m-32-01.s.s2.hint.0: Write the difference x³−x as one expression and find x values making it 0.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.hint.1: Try another value, such as x=2.5 or x=−2, and see whether the difference is 0.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.o.a: x³−x=x(x−1)(x+1), so both sides match only when one factor is 0.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.r.a: You factored the difference and found where both sides match.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.o.b: x³ is always greater than x, so the values where they match can be decided separately.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.r.b: Compare x³ and x directly when x is between 0 and 1 or negative. It is not always greater.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.o.c: 2 is an integer, so calculation fails there, unlike at 0, 1, and −1.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.r.c: 2 is an integer too. It doesn't work because it is an integer.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.o.d: A non-identity equation always works for exactly 3 values.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.r.d: The number of solutions differs by equation. For example, x²=x works for 2 values.
y-m-32-01.s.s2.explain: x³−x=x(x−1)(x+1), so it is 0 only for x=0, 1, −1. At any other value the sides differ; for x=2, 8≠2.

y-m-32-03.prereq.2: (Assumption) H1 here only means difficulty/support, not grade curriculum. Assumed intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit after middle school multiplication formulas, factoring, quadratic basics.
y-m-32-03.title: If an expression is never 0, does that mean it cannot be factored?
y-m-32-03.topic: Factoring: decide when there is no linear factor
y-m-32-03.goal: Sort what 'no real value makes it 0' proves and what it doesn't; update your judgment when a new form of the expression appears.
y-m-32-03.material: Minho sees x⁴+4 and says, "Whatever real x I substitute, x⁴+4 is never 0, so it can't be factored further." (x⁴ means x to the fourth power. Here factoring means writing it as a product of polynomials with integer coefficients.) Evaluate his conclusion.
y-m-32-03.thinking.0: Tell apart the range supported by evidence
y-m-32-03.thinking.1: Update your judgment with new information
y-m-32-03.prereq.0: Difference of squares formula A²−B²=(A+B)(A−B) (middle-school level)
y-m-32-03.prereq.1: Calculate by multiplying and expanding polynomials
y-m-32-03.s.s1.prompt: New information appears one part at a time. Each time, choose what you think about Minho's conclusion.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.hint.0: Is a step missing between Minho's observation (never 0 for real x) and conclusion (cannot be factored)?
y-m-32-03.s.s1.hint.1: Tell whether new information changes the observation or the basis for the conclusion.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.info: Putting x=0, 1, −1, 2 gives x⁴+4 values 4, 5, 5, 20. For every real x, x⁴≥0, so x⁴+4≥4.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: What do you think of Minho's conclusion from this information?
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.after: No real x makes it 0, so there is no factor x−k. Whether it can be a product of two quadratic expressions must be checked separately, so his conclusion is premature.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.o.a: We confirmed there is no real root, so we can be certain it can't be factored.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Having no linear factor differs from being unable to write it as any product.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Being at least 4 has nothing to do with whether it can be factored.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: If there were a linear factor x−k, the value at x=k would be 0, so this is relevant.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.o.c: A large value suggests it can be neatly split into factors.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: There is no basis for linking value size with factorability.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.o.d: It shows there is no linear factor, but a product of two quadratics may still be possible.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You separated what the observation shows (no linear factor) from the conclusion (cannot be factored).
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.info: Rewrite x⁴+4 as (x²+2)²−(2x)². Since (x²+2)²=x⁴+4x²+4 and (2x)²=4x², their difference is x⁴+4.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: What do you think of this new form?
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.after: Both judgments are reasonable. In A²−B²=(A+B)(A−B), set A=x²+2 and B=2x; it may become a product of quadratics. Check next.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.o.a: It's the same expression in a different form, so nothing new is learned.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: A new form of the same expression can show which formula applies.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.o.b: (x²+2)(2x), that is, (x²+2) multiplied by (2x), is exactly the same as x⁴+4. The number 2 appears in both factors.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Difference of squares factors into the sum times the difference, not the two expressions themselves. Expand to check.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.o.c: It looks like a difference of squares, so it may factor, but don't settle it before expanding.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: This uses a plausible form as a clue but checks before deciding.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.o.d: It is a difference of squares, so it is a product of sum and difference.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.1.r.d: You recognized A²−B² and recalled the formula. Now check that the two quadratic factors are right.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.info: Expanding (x²+2x+2)(x²−2x+2) gives x⁴+4. (The x³ and x terms cancel.)
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: What is your final judgment on Minho's conclusion?
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.after: A product form exists, so Minho is wrong. But 'there is no real root' is correct and means no linear factor. These are judgments at different levels of detail.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Minho is right: the quadratics cannot be factored further, so x⁴+4 cannot be factored.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: It is already a product, so x⁴+4 has been factored. Whether each quadratic can be split further is separate.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.o.b: The value was at least 4, so this expansion must be wrong.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Substitution only shows no linear factor. Check expansion by direct calculation.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.o.c: No real root is correct, but concluding 'cannot be factored' from it is wrong.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: This precise judgment accepts the observation and fixes only the leap.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Minho is wrong. x⁴+4 can be written as a product of two quadratic expressions.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You disproved the conclusion by showing the actual product form.
y-m-32-03.s.s1.reflect: If you chose 'premature' in step 1, how did step 3 confirm it? Say what factor 'no value makes it 0' rules out and what remains possible.
y-m-32-03.s.s2.prompt: Imagine explaining to Minho. Separate the correct observation from the part of his conclusion that needs correction.
y-m-32-03.s.s2.hint.0: Separate Minho's two statements: the observation and the conclusion.
y-m-32-03.s.s2.hint.1: Write one expression line you could use to refute the conclusion.
y-m-32-03.s.s2.placeholder: Example: Your observation is right. ... But ...
y-m-32-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you separate the correct observation from the leap?
y-m-32-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you show with an expression why it can be factored?
y-m-32-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you explain the difference between 'no linear factor' and 'cannot be factored'?
y-m-32-03.s.s2.model.0: Your observation is right: for every real x, x⁴+4≥4, so it never equals 0 and has no linear factor x−k. But the conclusion needs correction. It can still be a product of quadratics: (x²+2x+2)(x²−2x+2).
y-m-32-03.s.s2.model.1: There is no real root, so there is no linear factor. But x⁴+4=(x²+2)²−(2x)² is a difference of squares and becomes two quadratic factors, so 'cannot be factored' needs correction.

y-m-32-06.prereq.2: (Assumption) H1 here only means difficulty/support, not grade curriculum. Assumed intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit after middle school multiplication formulas, factoring, quadratic basics.
y-m-32-06.title: Compare four ways to find a remainder
y-m-32-06.topic: Compare and check different remainder methods
y-m-32-06.goal: Compare methods for same remainder problem; separate valid methods from leaps, judge convenience when method changes, and check result.
y-m-32-06.material: Find remainder when f(x)=x²⁰−3x+2 divided by x²−1. f=(x²−1)Q+R, Q integer-coefficient polynomial. Five methods: A: R=ax+b; plug x=1,−1 to get f(1)=a+b and f(−1)=−a+b; solve a,b. B: Since x²=1, set x²⁰=(x²)¹⁰=1, so f=−3x+3. C: Since f(1)=0, f(−1)=6, take average 3 as remainder. D: Long-divide degree 20 fully. E: f(1)=0, so divisible by x−1; assume divisible by x²−1 too, remainder 0. [2 20 3]
y-m-32-06.thinking.1: Find leap in plausible but wrong method
y-m-32-06.prereq.0: Remainder after quadratic division can be ax+b; calculate f(k) (intro high-school polynomial unit)
y-m-32-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose all methods giving correct remainder (include slow but correct).
y-m-32-06.s.s1.hint.0: For each method, write one line showing starting fact (division equation, substitution).
y-m-32-06.s.s1.hint.1: Plug f(1),f(−1) from C/E into remainder ax+b and check.
y-m-32-06.s.s1.r.a: f(1)=0 and f(−1)=6 correct, but why average become remainder? Put x=1 and −1 in ax+b.
y-m-32-06.s.s1.r.b: This writes remainder ax+b and plugs values making divisor 0 to find a,b.
y-m-32-06.s.s1.o.c: Method E (since divisible by x−1, remainder 0)
y-m-32-06.s.s1.r.c: Is divisible by x−1 same as x²−1? Check f(−1).
y-m-32-06.s.s1.r.d: Uses x²=1 at values making x²−1 zero. [0]
y-m-32-06.s.s1.r.e: Full long division give correct remainder but takes long.
y-m-32-06.s.s1.explain: A and B use roots (1,−1) of divisor and get R=−3x+3. D slow but correct. C has no reason average f(1),f(−1) is remainder. E has f(−1)=6, so not divisible by x+1. [0]
y-m-32-06.s.s2.prompt: If divisor change from x²−1 to x²−3x+2=(x−1)(x−2), what happen to A and B? Say which choose and why.
y-m-32-06.s.s2.hint.0: First write how many x values make new divisor 0.
y-m-32-06.s.s2.hint.1: In B, what replace x² with, and what happen to x³?
y-m-32-06.s.s2.placeholder: e.g. Method A ..., Method B ..., so ...
y-m-32-06.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You explain why A works same with new divisor?
y-m-32-06.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You explain why B becomes hard with new divisor?
y-m-32-06.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Your reason connect to method range (can it always be used)?
y-m-32-06.s.s2.model.0: Even with divisor (x−1)(x−2), A works same: plug x=1,2 to get f(1)=a+b and f(2)=2a+b. B must use x²=3x−2 to reduce x²⁰, awkward. I choose A. [1 2 20]
y-m-32-06.s.s2.model.1: B fast because special x²=1. New divisor gives x²=3x−2; keep replacing x³,x⁴,..., complicated. Generally A is safe: write ax+b and use f(1),f(2), but for simple x²−1 B is fine too.
y-m-32-06.s.s3.prompt: After finding R=−3x+3, how check something that must be true if R correct?
y-m-32-06.s.s3.hint.0: Move R to one side of division equation and see what remaining expression is multiple of.
y-m-32-06.s.s3.hint.1: Put suitable integer x, find x²−1, check relation with f(x)−R(x).
y-m-32-06.s.s3.o.a: Put x=3 and check f(3) multiple of 8
y-m-32-06.s.s3.r.a: If remainder nonzero, does f(3) itself need be multiple of 8? [0]
y-m-32-06.s.s3.o.b: Put x=3 and check f(3)−R(3) multiple of 8
y-m-32-06.s.s3.r.b: From division equation f−R=(x²−1)Q. At x=3, x²−1=8.
y-m-32-06.s.s3.o.c: Check R(3) natural and less than 8
y-m-32-06.s.s3.r.c: Remainder is degree condition, no requirement value natural/less divisor value.
y-m-32-06.s.s3.explain: f−R=(x²−1)Q, and Q integer coefficients, so at x=3 f(3)−R(3) is 8×integer. Indeed f(3)−R(3)=3486784400=8×435848050. f(3)=3486784394 leaves remainder 2 on division by 8, not multiple, so A wrong. [8]

y-m-32-08.prereq.2: (Assumption) H1 here only means difficulty/support, not grade curriculum. Assumed intro high-school Common Math polynomial unit after middle school multiplication formulas, factoring, quadratic basics.
y-m-32-08.title: Which b values make x²+bx+12 factor?
y-m-32-08.topic: Factor quadratic expressions and number range (integers/reals)
y-m-32-08.goal: Systematically make quadratic expressions wey factor into product of linear expressions with integer coefficients; distinguish say missing case in list no necessarily 'impossible' but fit depend on number range.
y-m-32-08.material: For quadratic expression x²+bx+12, b na integer. You wan find b values wey make expression factor as (x+m)(x+n). (x² mean 'x squared'.) First look only at case where m and n na integers.
y-m-32-08.thinking.0: Find every solution within a limit without missing any
y-m-32-08.thinking.1: Separate conclusions wey depend on range (integers/reals)
y-m-32-08.prereq.1: Sign of discriminant b²−4ac of quadratic equation and real roots (from middle-school 3rd year to high-school Common Math level)
y-m-32-08.s.s1.prompt: Find integer m and n wey make (x+m)(x+n)=x²+bx+12 and give resulting b, using 4 different b values. (Pairs wey only swap m and n positions give same b, count dem as one.)
y-m-32-08.s.s1.hint.0: Compare coefficients term by term for expanded x²+(m+n)x+mn and x²+bx+12.
y-m-32-08.s.s1.hint.1: Find integer pairs with product 12, starting from smallest, and calculate their sums.
y-m-32-08.s.s1.ok.c1: m, n and b na integers.
y-m-32-08.s.s1.fail.c1: m, n and b gats be integers.
y-m-32-08.s.s1.fail.c2: Product m and n no be 12. Compare with constant term 12.
y-m-32-08.s.s1.ok.c3: Sum of m and n na b.
y-m-32-08.s.s1.fail.c3: Sum of m and n no be b. Compare with x coefficient.
y-m-32-08.s.s1.explain: Since (x+m)(x+n)=x²+(m+n)x+mn, we get mn=12 and b=m+n. Integer pairs with product 12 na (1, 12), (2, 6), (3, 4), plus pairs where both negative. So b fit get six values: ±7, ±8, ±13.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.prompt: b=9 no dey list. Yeonghui talk, 'x²+9x+12 no fit factor.' Wetin you think about this claim?
y-m-32-08.s.s2.hint.0: First look for integer pair whose product na 12 and sum na 9.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.hint.1: Calculate discriminant of x²+9x+12=0 and check its sign.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.o.a: x²+9x+12 factor as (x+3)(x+4), so Yeonghui claim wrong.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.r.a: When you expand (x+3)(x+4), check x coefficient.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.o.b: Integer coefficients no fit do am, but discriminant positive, so e fit factor with real numbers.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.r.b: This point out say whether e fit factor depend on 'which number range' question ask about.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.o.c: E no fit factor with integers or real numbers, so Yeonghui claim correct.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.o.d: Whether it fit factor depend only on constant term 12, no matter b.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.r.d: Even with same constant term, result change when b change.
y-m-32-08.s.s2.explain: Discriminant of x²+9x+12=0 na 81−48=33>0, so e get two real roots and fit write as (x−α)(x−β) using real numbers. With integer coefficients, no integer pair get product 12 and sum 9, so e no fit do am. So Yeonghui claim correct only for 'integer range'.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.prompt: If we allow product of linear expressions with 'real coefficients' instead of only 'integer coefficients', which integer b values make x²+bx+12 factor?
y-m-32-08.s.s3.hint.0: Find sign of b²−48 for b=6 and b=7.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.hint.1: On number line, find range of integer b wey satisfy b²−48≥0.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.o.a: E possible only for earlier values like b=±7, ±8, ±13, no other b.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.r.a: Before, we allow only integer m and n. Check wetin happen when allowed numbers range widen.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.o.b: We widen range to real numbers, so e fit factor for every integer b.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.r.b: If b=6, discriminant na 36−48. Check the sign.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.o.c: Integer b values wey make b²−48 0 or more: b≥7 or b≤−7.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.r.c: This express factorability condition by connecting am to discriminant sign.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.o.d: E fit factor only when b even integer.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.r.d: E factor for odd value like b=7 too.
y-m-32-08.s.s3.explain: For factorization using real numbers, real roots gats exist, so b²−48≥0. If b²≥48, |b|≥7, therefore integer b na 7 or higher, or −7 or lower. From b=−6 to 6, no factorization even with real numbers.

y-m-32-09.title: Even if equation true, e fit still fail as result of division?
y-m-32-09.topic: Conditions for quotient and remainder in polynomial division
y-m-32-09.goal: Show say equation 'f=(divisor)×(quotient)+(remainder)' being true no enough to call those quotient and remainder; understand why remainder degree condition needed to fix one answer.
y-m-32-09.material: This question divide f(x)=x³+2x+1 by x−1. Jiho say 'quotient x²+x+3, remainder 4'; Sua say 'quotient x²+x+2, remainder x+3'. Both expand and check say f(x)=(x−1)×(quotient)+(remainder) hold. (x³ mean 'x cubed'.)
y-m-32-09.thinking.0: Sort out whether equation na necessary or enough condition
y-m-32-09.thinking.1: Make examples wey break condition yourself
y-m-32-09.thinking.2: Explain why condition fix one solution
y-m-32-09.prereq.0: Multiply and add polynomials, and combine like terms
y-m-32-09.prereq.1: Rule for division equation A=BQ+R: degree of R gats be less than degree of B (intro level of high-school Common Math polynomial unit)
y-m-32-09.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think about Sua answer?
y-m-32-09.s.s1.hint.0: For each person, multiply quotient by (x−1), add remainder and check if result equal f.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.hint.1: Put Jiho and Sua remainders side by side, compare each one with divisor x−1, and note any obvious difference.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.o.a: Equation hold, so both answers be valid quotients and remainders; many choices fit.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.r.a: Think whether checking equation true na the same as checking whether 'dem count as accepted quotient and remainder'.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.o.b: Jiho answer with bigger quotient correct.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.r.b: Quotient size no be criterion. Both quotients only different in constant term.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.o.c: Remainder gats be 0, so Jiho and Sua both wrong.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.r.c: Remainder only 0 if division exact. Find f(1) and check whether e divide by x−1.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.o.d: We confirm equation hold, but we gats check degree condition for remainder too.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.r.d: This asks whether extra condition needed to accept result, beyond checking equation.
y-m-32-09.s.s1.explain: Remainder degree gats be less than divisor degree. Sua remainder x+3 get same degree as divisor x−1, so e break condition. Therefore Sua equation true but e no count as 'division result'.
y-m-32-09.s.s2.prompt: Like Sua, write quotient as x²+x+k and remainder as px+q. Find 3 different (k,p,q) sets wey make f(x)=(x−1)(x²+x+k)+px+q hold with p≠0. (k na integer.)
y-m-32-09.s.s2.hint.0: Expand (x−1)(x²+x+k) and subtract am from f(x).
y-m-32-09.s.s2.hint.1: Fix one k and make table showing how x coefficient and constant term of remainder change.
y-m-32-09.s.s2.ok.c2: x coefficient correct, so equation hold.
y-m-32-09.s.s2.fail.c2: x coefficient no correct. Expand (x−1)(x²+x+k) and compare its x coefficient with f.
y-m-32-09.s.s2.ok.c3: Constant term correct, so equation hold.
y-m-32-09.s.s2.fail.c3: Constant term no correct. Compare constant term in expanded expression with f.
y-m-32-09.s.s2.ok.c4: This example get linear remainder, so no count as division result.
y-m-32-09.s.s2.fail.c4: If p=0, remainder constant, so e be valid division result. This time find examples with p≠0.
y-m-32-09.s.s2.explain: (x−1)(x²+x+k)=x³+(k−1)x−k; subtracting from f gives remainder (3−k)x+(1+k). So p=3−k and q=1+k. If k=2, remainder na x+3 (Sua answer); if k=0, e na 3x+1; if k=1, e na 2x+2. Only when k=3 p become 0, wey na Jiho answer.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.prompt: How many k values make p=0, and what role condition 'remainder degree less than divisor' get for that?
y-m-32-09.s.s3.hint.0: From p=3−k, find k value wey make p=0.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.hint.1: Check if examples with p≠0 wey you make earlier satisfy the condition.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.o.a: Only k=3 dey, so adding this condition fix quotient and remainder as one answer.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.r.a: This judgment connect number of k values with p=0 to uniqueness.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.o.b: Two values, k=2 and k=3, so both accepted under this condition.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.o.c: No such k dey, so no quotient fit satisfy condition.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.r.c: Put Jiho answer into this form.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.o.d: Only k=3 dey, but answers with p≠0 still have same status, so several remain.
y-m-32-09.s.s3.r.d: You check earlier step wetin criterion determine the status be?
y-m-32-09.s.s3.explain: If p=3−k=0, only k=3 dey. So adding condition 'remainder degree less than divisor degree' fix quotient x²+x+3 and remainder 4 as one answer. Equation alone no decide am.
